text: May 6, 2026 - Western research into the history of Tibetan music has often focused more on religious than secular musics. title: Hlersu language — Grokipedia
text: Hlersu (also known as Lesu, Sansu, or Shansu) is a Loloish language spoken by approximately 15,700 members of the Shansu subgroup of the Yi ethnic group in Yunnan Province, China (as of 2013). [1] It is classified within the Sino-Tibetan language family, specifically under the Tibeto-Burman branch and the Central Ngwi subgroup. text: Hlersu is an endangered indigenous language of China. It belongs to the Sino-Tibetan language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools.

title: Understanding the importance of Tibetan music
text: May 6, 2025 - You will find that flutes and lutes combine with some percussion beats to create a soft aroma of music that is thought to resemble a constant communication link with the divine world, one that only "perfect beings" are able to compose. It is officially named Sino-Mongolian music and is heard in the streets during festivals and parties.
